title: Hybrid sync/async tool invocation semantics with schema versioning and frame checkpoints (acceptance criteria)
creator: Anika Rao
description: Scope: Define and accept the behavior for mixed synchronous and asynchronous tool invocations when the model is emitting structured partial output (frames). This ticket covers schema version negotiation, durable frame checkpoints (resume tokens), idempotency of tool calls, billing attribution for hybrid flows, backpressure behavior when downstream tools are slow, and required telemetry/alerts. Background: multiple customers have requested deterministic, resumable streamed outputs where tool results can be awaited inline (sync) or deferred (async) without breaking schema expectations or causing duplicate side-effects. This PRD clarifies acceptance criteria for engineering to implement and QA to validate.
acceptance_criteria: Schema negotiation: every stream must begin with a machine-readable header frame containing schema_id and schema_version. If consumer and runtime disagree on version, runtime must emit a single compatibility decision frame (accept|degrade|reject) and follow fallback rules.

Frame-level validation: each emitted frame must validate against the active schema version within the runtime; validation failures are surfaced as structured error frames (error_code + human_reason + debug_id) and do not close the stream unless marked fatal.

Sync tool semantics: synchronous tool calls (tool.invoke_sync) invoked inline block further dependent frames until tool response is returned; the runtime must guarantee at-most-once side-effect semantics when the model requests retry on transient errors using idempotency keys.

Async tool semantics: asynchronous tool calls (tool.enqueue_async) return a persistent tool_call_id immediately; subsequent frames may continue but must reference the tool_call_id. The runtime must provide a standard polling/notification mechanism so the model/consumer can receive the eventual tool result and reconcile frames.

Resume/checkpoint tokens: every stable frame boundary must include an optional resume_token. Resume tokens must be monotonic, cryptographically signed by the control plane, and sufficient to resume from that exact stream position (including outstanding async tool_call_ids). Resuming a stream must result in deterministic frame emission identical to the original run when no external inputs changed.

Idempotency and replays: tool invocations must accept an idempotency_key. If a client or runtime replays a frame with the same idempotency_key, the downstream tool must not perform duplicate side effects. The system should default to safe retries and provide error classes for non-retryable conflicts.

Backpressure and flow control: when downstream tools are rate limited or delayed beyond a configurable threshold, the runtime must emit a warning_frame and either (a) pause model emission until capacity returns, or (b) switch to a degraded fallback schema path if allowed by schema negotiation. Flow-control decisions must be visible in the console and metrics.

Billing attribution: metering must attribute costs to the combination of model tokens + tool invocation units. For async tool flows where a tool result arrives later, billing events must be correlated via tool_call_id and shown in per-route cost breakdowns.

Observability and telemetry: each important event (schema negotiation result, checkpoint created, tool_invoke_attempt, tool_invoke_result, resume_attempt, validation_failure) must emit structured telemetry with debug_id and be queryable in the console for at least 30 days by default.

Failure recovery: simulated failures (tool crash, network partition, control-plane restart) must allow a resumed client using a valid resume_token to reach a consistent recovery state or receive a clear fatal error frame with recovery instructions.

E2E test coverage: automated tests must cover sync success, sync transient failure with retry, async enqueue->result, resume after partial emission, idempotency verification against duplicate invocations, and billing attribution verification. Tests must be part of the CI gating for canary rollout.

Canary & rollout gates: rollout to 5% of traffic requires zero critical regressions for 48 hours in latency and error-rate SLAs (per-route); promotion to 25% requires 7 days without regression and successful credit-card customer pilot verifying resume and async flows.
Documentation: public API docs and SDK examples for sync and async patterns plus a migration guide for customers must be published prior to GA (docs links in spec_links).
implementation_notes: Prefer signed resume tokens emitted from control plane to avoid client-side token forging; tokens contain minimal checkpoint metadata and references to outstanding async tool_call_ids.
Default idempotency_key generation: use stream_id + monotonic_frame_index + optional client_provided_key to tie retries to a stable identity.
Trade-off: synchronous tool calls simplify consumer semantics but increase tail latency; provide policy to convert blocking calls to async with a recommended UX pattern in SDKs.
Use existing telemetry schema (event_type, stream_id, debug_id, tags) to minimize console work; expand retention for critical debugging windows as an opt-in enterprise setting.
Billing: ensure storage of tool_call_id->billing_event for 90 days to reconcile late-arriving async results in customer invoices.
Security: security_review_required flagged because resume tokens and tool_call_ids are sensitive; encryption-at-rest and scoped access required for private deployments.
qa_checklist: Run CI e2e suite described in acceptance_criteria on runtime branch and confirm green
Execute chaos tests: kill tool worker mid-invocation and validate resume behavior
Verify idempotency by replaying frames with same idempotency_key and confirming single side-effect
Validate console shows per-route billing for sample async flows for last 7 days
Confirm docs and SDK snippets render correctly in docs site and examples repo
